rows.t: A failed load was console-only and the page looked empty (TD-36's sibling); the error alert now says what failed.

A native date input draws the browser's locale (month first under en-US, "2026/10/14" or "12月31日" elsewhere) and cannot be reformatted; the DateTimeField shows and reads one format whatever the browser (C3, `§ Dates, times and numbers › The date control`). Inside the range picker's popover the calendar is the popover's own month grid, so the two date fields are the typed part only (the text-only variant, no second popover); min and max keep disabling days outside the range.

A native time input follows the browser's 12- or 24-hour habit; the DateTimeField reads and shows HH:mm on the 24-hour clock (C3). The start and end time fields of the range picker (text-only variant).

The custom range label is built by date-fns with the month first and no year ("Oct 1 – Oct 7"). One format: `D MMM – D MMM YYYY`, an en dash, the year once at the end and twice when the years differ ("28 Dec 2025 – 3 Jan 2026"). A preset shows its own label ("Last 7 days").
Where the label is shown: the period button's text (`:169`) and, inside "Select analytics period: {range}", its accessible name (`:145`). Both read the format above.

The popover's month title and the grid's accessible name (`:304`, `:328`) are built by date-fns from the `locale` prop. They read the fixed English table instead: `MMMM YYYY`, the full month name and the year. In English the text is the same; what changes is that no locale can alter it.
Each day button's accessible name (`:383`): day first like every date here, with the full month name from the fixed table: `D MMMM YYYY`.
The weekday headings (`:343`) are the first letter of the weekday's name in the fixed table: S, M, T, W, T, F, S.
Their accessible names (`:335`) are the full names from the same table, Sunday to Saturday. The popover no longer reads `locale`; the week starts where `weekStartsOn` says (Sunday today).
`{durationInHours}` is `{hours}`; exactly 1 reads "1 hour", a fraction takes the plural (1.5 hours).
Analytics sessions (one run of a user's activity); 1 session.
Model tokens, the unit of usage on this page; 1 token.
1 interaction.
`{data.usage}` is `{usage}`; 1 request.

The empty-value glyph stays an em dash, because a lone dash that stands for "no value" is a glyph, not punctuation (C5, DS.53), and takes the accessible name "No value" (DS.54). Three places: a user's session count (`:305`), and a session's end time in the expanded row (`:426`) and in the sessions table (`:484`).
